**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/eu-frames-one-day-data-tools.html#/part-1-credibility-as-a-software-problem){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 1 opens briefly on credibility: the three operations that go under the word 'replication', and the five Multi100 analysts of one claim who disagreed, but whose disagreement could be diagnosed afterwards because every one of them shipped a document that somebody else could run. The rest of the part lays out the toolchain that makes that kind of checking possible, and ends with R running on every machine.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the opening | The plan of the day, the two kinds of aim, and what you do not need. Open the browser lab in a tab and leave it to load. | 6 minutes |
| Slides, the vocabulary | The matrix of data and analysis that separates reproduction, robustness and replication; repeatability and credibility; a quick check on the matrix in peer review; the practices of open research. | 12 minutes |
| Slides, Multi100 from the inside | What an analyst received, the paper in brief, the two Multi100 tasks and the common scale, a forest plot of the five analysts, and the software and document format that each of them used. | 14 minutes |
| Slides, the toolchain, with [Positron, RStudio and VS Code](../../companion/ide.qmd), [Quarto and reproducible documents](../../companion/quarto.qmd) and [Git and GitHub](../../companion/git-github.qmd) as companions | Open-source software; the map of the tools; programming languages; editors and IDEs; plain-text file formats and what happens when a document renders; the package layer; version control; where data and code are archived; licences. | 32 minutes |
| Slides on the browser lab, then [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) Task 1, or the check script of the workspace | Get to the point where a line of R runs and the panel of 270 country-years is in front of you. | 26 minutes with the slides, and the 30-minute break after it if you need more |

**By the end of the part** R runs on your machine, you can tell apart the three operations that go under the word 'replication', and you can place any tool that someone names on the map of the toolchain.
